short: How teams exchanged and verified candidate circuits

statements.markdown: All large-scale experimental runs of autonomous discovery
statements.note: The authors used Gemini 4 Carbon for the large-scale autonomous discovery runs. The reporting here concerns which model generated candidates. Acceptance of those candidates used the Lean checks described in Appendix B.

statements.markdown: idea notes are reviewed summaries rather than formal proofs
statements.note: The wiki stored verified solutions, helper Lean files that could be reused, and reviewed notes on ideas. Section 2.6 gives an example of a helper first imported by one team and then reused by another team’s stopping-power run. The authors also report that one dead-end note stopped two later proposals.

statements.markdown: teams convene periodically every four hours
statements.note: Teams exchanged proposals and questions in a shared forum every four hours. In Fig. S5, Team 3 proposed a $109$-Toffoli subroutine with blocks of $47$, $15$, and $47$ Toffolis. Team 1 suggested proving the conjugation identity before substituting the clean ancillas, which would avoid repeating the proof for all $47$ inverse operations.

statements.markdown: cost projections posted in a conference carry no weight until independently verified
statements.note: Appendix C gives the rule for admitting a verified candidate to the shared wiki. The default requires a cost reduction of at least $5\%$. For an established solution, the authors also accepted a strictly cheaper candidate with at least $20\%$ less Lean code.
